items.entity: volume bound V in Σρ_i = V (CANT-16-2-2-5)
items.description: Problem (1) requires Σρ_i = V, but Sec. 7, Sec. 7.1 and Table 1 never give V (or V/m) for this example. V only shows up indirectly, through the starting guess ρ_i = V/m (Secs. 3.2 and 4.1). So the effective volume fraction V/(m·ρ̄) is unknown.
readings: V = 0.1·m (10% of the fully solid volume, with ρ̄ = 1)

items.description: No number is ever given for the upper bound ρ̄ in (1), which is also used in the DOC update (Alg. 4, line 6) and the duality gap (7). Sec. 1 only says ρ̄ > ρ̲ and that the problem is strictly feasible. Sec. 7.1 gives only lower bounds. Sec. 7.2 says solid elements cluster along the boundary, which suggests ρ̄ is active, so its value together with V decides which elements are fully solid.
readings: ρ̄_i = 1 for every element (standard; fits the ρ_i > 0.1 plotting threshold in Fig. 3)
no active upper bound (ρ̄ very large, pure VTS)
some other finite uniform value, which changes the effective fraction V/(m·ρ̄)

items.entity: lower density bound ρ̲ (stiffness of empty elements)
items.description: Sec. 7.1 gives different lower bounds for the same example: ρ̲ = 0 for PBM, ρ̲ = 1e-7 for IP and DOC, plus an extra IP run with ρ̲ = 1e-3, whose objective (66.1988863) differs from the others (≈66.19273). A standard displacement-based solver needs ρ̲ > 0 because K(ρ) is singular otherwise, so the value to use is not unique.
readings: ρ̲ = 0 (the PBM setting; only usable with a dual/PBM-type solver)

items.description: Sec. 6.2 says only that the elements are hexahedral with trilinear basis functions. No Young's modulus for the element matrices K_i appears anywhere, including Sec. 7 and Table 1.

items.entity: Poisson's ratio ν (isotropic linear elastic material assumed)
items.description: The text never gives a Poisson's ratio for the element stiffness matrices K_i. It also never states that the material is isotropic.

items.entity: z-direction load on the right-hand face
items.description: Sec. 7 says only that 'a load in direction z is applied in the middle of the right-hand face'. No force or traction magnitude is given. Fig. 2(a), which is said to hold the specifications, is not available.

items.entity: z-load at the middle of the right-hand (x = L) face
items.description: Sec. 7 says 'a load in direction z is applied in the middle of the right-hand face (Figure 2(a))'. Whether this is a single nodal force at the face centre or is spread along a line or over a small centred patch is shown only in Fig. 2(a). By contrast, the bridge load is described explicitly as a uniform load on a centred rectangle.
readings: single nodal force at the face-centre node (x = L, y = W/2, z = H/2); this node exists on every mesh level
line load along the full width (y-direction) at mid-height z = H/2
line load along the full height (z-direction) at mid-width y = W/2
uniform traction on a small square patch centred on the face (e.g. 2×2 or 4×4 fine elements)

items.entity: physical size of the 16×2×2 cuboid / element edge length
items.description: Sec. 7 defines the domain as m_x×m_y×m_z 'cubes of equal size'. That fixes the 16:2:2 proportions and, at level 5, a 256×32×32 element mesh. The edge length of the cubes, and so the absolute dimensions, is never given. Because V = Σρ_i has no units, this only rescales the compliance.
readings: coarse cubes of unit edge: domain 16×2×2, fine-element edge 1/16
fine elements of unit edge: domain 256×32×32

items.description: No filter or filter radius is mentioned anywhere. Algorithms 1, 3 and 4 work on raw element densities, and the VTS problem is convex. However, the DOC is described as 'adapted' from top88.m, which filters sensitivities or densities, and the text never says explicitly that no filter was used.
readings: top88-style density filter with r_min ≈ 1.5 fine elements
top88-style sensitivity filter with r_min ≈ 1.5 fine elements

items.entity: stopping criterion that defines the reference result
items.description: Table 1 reports seven runs of this example: PBM at 1e-5 and 1e-6; IP at 1e-5 with ρ̲ = 1e-7 or 1e-3; and DOC with ε_DOC = 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-5 (q = 0.5, τ_α = 0.1·ε_DOC). Sec. 7.1 and Fig. 3 show that ε_DOC = 1e-2 and 1e-3 give visibly different layouts from the converged one. Those images are only for the smaller CANT-16-2-2-4. So it is unclear which stopping criterion a re-run should use.
readings: converge tightly (DOC ε_DOC = 1e-5 or PBM 1e-6; ½fᵀu ≈ 66.19273)

items.entity: starting design and move limit for the OC/DOC method
items.description: Starting densities are given only for PBM and IP (ρ_i = V/m, Secs. 3.2 and 4.1), not for DOC. Algorithm 4 has no move limit, even though it is 'adapted' from top88.m, which uses move = 0.2. These choices change the path of the iterations and the result at loose ε_DOC, but not the converged optimum of the convex problem.
readings: uniform ρ_i = V/m with no move limit (as written in Alg. 4)
uniform ρ_i = V/m with the top88 move limit of 0.2
